claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons are dominated by enhanced magnetoelastic coupling at nanoscale domain boundaries.
Nanoscale confinement increases internal stresses in these FeMnNiGeSi structures.
Nanoscale confinement alters the energy barrier for magnetic phase transitions.
Heat-transfer limitations slow the attainable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Confinement-related stress and heat-transfer limitations produce broader hysteresis and a diluted magnetocaloric effect relative to bulk samples.
The as-deposited films and nanoribbons possess a deposition-derived network of defects and domain boundaries.
A controlled low-temperature post-deposition anneal will partially relieve residual stresses.
A controlled low-temperature post-deposition anneal will modify nanoscale domain-boundary structure.
The relevant magnetic transition occurs at approximately 300–350 K.
The proposed behavior applies under magnetic fields below 1 T.
The nanoscale domain boundaries and associated magnetoelastic strain fields arise from residual stress and defects in the as-deposited state.
Annealing-induced stress reduction and domain-boundary modification lower the magnetic-phase-transition energy barrier.
Lowering the magnetic transition barrier narrows hysteresis.
Lowering the magnetic transition barrier enhances the effective magnetocaloric response despite confinement and heat-transfer limitations.
Annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a sharper and more pronounced magnetocaloric temperature change than the as-deposited baseline.
As-deposited samples exhibit pronounced hysteresis and a smeared magnetocaloric response because of high internal stress and suboptimal domain-boundary configurations.
The magnitude of annealing-induced improvement is uncertain because residual structural disorder and nanoscale domain configurations may compete.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says heat-transfer limitations slow or limit cycle frequency, which implies an upper bound on usable frequency, whereas the boundary field says they set a lower bound on cycle frequency.
